statement: enforcer_domain::ids::RuleId's validator (validate_rule_id in crates/enforcer-domain/src/ids.rs) requires the PREFIX segment before the first `-` to be pure uppercase-alnum with no internal dash -- a ruleId like `AGENTS-CHAIN-RESOLVES` fails to parse because the parser reads `AGENTS` as the prefix and then requires every remaining dash-separated segment to be alnum-or-dot only, so `CHAIN-RESOLVES` splits into two segments and the second one (`RESOLVES`) is fine alone but the intended single-word-with-dashes rule family name never round-trips.
why: The workpack's own prose names example ruleIds like `AGENTS-CHAIN-RESOLVES`, `AGENTS-ROUTING-DECLARED`, `AGENTS-TREE-TERMINATES` verbatim, but those exact strings are NOT valid RuleId values under the existing brand -- multi-word rule-family names must be compressed into the segment-after-first-dash (e.g. `AGENTS-CHAIN.1`) the same way b02's own PLAN-* ids do (`PLAN-CAPSULE.1`, `PLAN-RESUME.1`), never taken as literal multi-dash prose.
howToApply: Before hardcoding any workpack-prose ruleId string into a `RuleId::from_str`/`.parse()` call or a fixture, always test-parse it first (or read enforcer-domain's validate_rule_id) -- workpack markdown prose freely invents readable multi-dash rule names that are not automatically valid brand values; pick the nearest single-prefix + `.N` suffix form instead (this pack used AGENTS-CHAIN.1 / AGENTS-ROUTING.1 / AGENTS-TREE.1 / AGENTS-BUDGET.1).

statement: ocentra_enforcer_coordination_claim MCP tool refuses writes (writeCompatible:false, reloadRequired:true) on a stale-loaded MCP process, and its `--paths` fallback CLI (scripts/rust-rules.mjs coordination claim) hard-rejects glob paths ('claim paths must be exact files, not folders or globs') even though the MCP schema's own `paths` field description implies arbitrary changed/claimed path strings.
why: A lane whose owns: line in its workpack is a glob (e.g. `tests/fixtures/agents_forest/**`) cannot claim that glob directly -- it must claim only the concrete files/paths it actually intends to create/touch under that glob, or the claim call fails closed with exit code 2.
howToApply: When a workpack's owns: field lists a `**` glob for a fixtures subtree, claim the concrete parent files you will create (module file, templates, lib.rs) and skip claiming the glob itself -- the fixture files under it are new paths with no prior claimant to conflict with anyway, so omitting them from the claim list does not create a real collision risk.

evidence.ref: ocentra_enforcer_run coordination-fallback claim error: 'claim paths must be exact files, not folders or globs: crates/enforcer-plan/tests/fixtures/agents_forest/**'
